headline: Alpine Tundra and Taiga Landscapes in the Charlevoix
reservation: Daily access to the park requires a SEPAQ entry permit, which should be purchased online in advance to guarantee entry during peak summer months. Camping and cabin stays within the park are managed through a separate high-demand reservation system; check the official SEPAQ portal for availability.

days.title: High Altitude Tundra Peaks

stops.name: Mont-du-Lac-des-Cygnes
stops.detail: Hike the park's most famous trail to a summit offering 360-degree views of the Charlevoix meteor crater.

stops.name: Le Pioui Trail
stops.detail: Traverse alpine ridges and lichen-covered landscapes that resemble the far northern Arctic tundra.

days.driving: Allow 60–90 minutes; conditions vary on mountain roads
days.note: Mountain weather is unpredictable; even in July, summit temperatures can be significantly lower than in the valley.

days.title: Lakes and Boreal Forests
days.start: Suggested: 9:00 AM from the Arthabaska Service Centre

stops.name: Lac Arthabaska
stops.detail: Rent a canoe or kayak to explore the quiet waters of this subarctic lake surrounded by dense spruce forest.

stops.name: La Tourbière Trail
stops.detail: Walk the boardwalks over an ancient peat bog to see unique carnivorous plants and resilient flora.

days.driving: Allow 40 minutes within the park; conditions vary by gravel road status
days.note: The interior park roads are partially gravel; drive slowly to avoid flying stones and protect the undercarriage.

days.title: Valleys and Flowing Waters
days.start: Suggested: 9:30 AM from the Thomas-Fortin Reception

stops.name: Rivière Malbaie
stops.detail: Observe the crystal-clear waters where fly-fishing for brook trout is a long-standing regional tradition.

stops.name: Le Boréal Trail
stops.detail: A gentle forest walk highlighting the transition between the mixed forest and the northern taiga.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; conditions vary with local traffic
days.note: Black flies and mosquitoes are prevalent in the forest areas during June and July.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Access
intel.text: The main park road (Route 381) is paved, but secondary access roads often open late in the spring due to snow. Check SEPAQ for official opening dates of the Arthabaska sector.

intel.title: Last Service Stations
intel.text: There is no fuel available inside the park. Ensure your tank is full before leaving Baie-Saint-Paul or Saint-Urbain.

intel.title: Limited Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular signal is non-existent in most of the park's valleys and trails. Emergency phones are located at the main visitor centers.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Parking at Mont-du-Lac-des-Cygnes is the most constrained in the park. On summer weekends, the lot may reach capacity, requiring a wait or a change of plans.

intel.title: Entry Permits
intel.text: The SEPAQ daily access fee is mandatory for all visitors. Physical passes are rarely sold on-site at smaller trailheads, so digital confirmation is essential.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental car at Quebec City (YQB) or Saguenay (YBG). Stop in Baie-Saint-Paul for regional provisions and outdoor supplies before driving the 30 minutes north to the park gates.
plan.vehicle: A standard vehicle is suitable for Route 381; however, an SUV is recommended for better clearance on secondary gravel roads leading to remote trailheads.
plan.goldenHour: The summit of Mont-du-Lac-des-Cygnes provides an expansive view of the St. Lawrence River during the early evening light.
